[docs/internal/database-connectors/row-level-security.md:48]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  For mysql and sqlite the claim holds. src/sqllens/safety/relations.py:125-138: `except RlsError: raise` passes refusals through, then `except Exception` logs with logger.warning(..., exc_info=True) and raises RlsError(f"row-level security could not verify {checked}; query blocked"). The try body includes _relations (sqlglot parse_one/traverse_scope) and _called_names (sqlglot tokenize), so parse/tokenize errors and lookup exceptions are covered. Mismatch: the doc (row-level-security.md:48) names "relation types" only for SQLite and gives the longer message everywhere else, but the code gives the shorter message for every non-mysql dialect. The same doc at line 44 says a statement under a no-entry dialect (anything but sqlite and mysql) that fails to parse is covered by this fail-closed paragraph. The doc is wrong for that case: it ties the shorter message to SQLite alone, and a no-entry dialect also runs no function-call check. Reach: shipped callers pass only mysql or sqlite (mysql/sql_runner.py:140, sqlite/sql_runner.py:211), but verify_base_tables is a public function and the doc itself describes the no-entry-dialect case. The impact is a wording imprecision in an internal doc.
